facts.F17: Carriers and owners, all test side in Lighthouse.Backend.Tests.Architecture (object_oriented): ReportsMembership (S1 support) holds the moving Reports types, each with its short name, its file, its layer from the closed choice ReportsLayer {Domain, Application, ApplicationMetrics}, its port-file flag, its old namespace and its new namespace Lighthouse.Backend.Modules.Reports.Domain, .Application or .Application.Metrics; the Reports types and files that stay (ReportRepository, the Models/Reports types, the three Reports controllers, ReportsControllerBase, ReportOwnerWriteAccess and the four API/DTO/Reports requests), each with namespace or path, owner and reason; and the targets found naming a moving type, each with file, target and kind (suppression, analyser, CI selection, test budget, host user, Stryker, log override). ReportsPatternRoles and ReportsStringsTheMoveRenames are S2 supports that feed the existing shared NamespaceMoveLaw (NamespaceMove, PatternRoleMap, PatternDeclaration, RoleBreak). No production carrier, effect, error type or per-process state changes; the only effects are reading the compiled production and test assemblies and repository text files; every failure is an NUnit assertion message stating WHAT, WHY and HOW.
facts.F18: Claim-to-checker: the membership and the preservation law are relations over a finite, closed domain (the compiled types of the production assembly, the const and static readonly string fields of the test assembly, two subjects per type, the string literals of the test project). They are executed exhaustively by native NUnit over the real IL. No Quint, TLA+ or Agda model: no state, transition, ordering, concurrency, time or unbounded input is claimed, so no checker install or waiver is needed. Property-based testing does not apply: closed finite domain, every case enumerated. Layers affected: only the test-side architecture rules (Infrastructure layer of the test project); production Domain, Application and Adapter layers are unchanged.
facts.F19: Shared law: REUSE. NamespaceMoveLaw already takes a move map and a pattern-role map (lifted by the Refinement packaging), so Reports adds its own map and calls the same law; no second law and no edit to NamespaceMoveLaw. The open renames of RoleBreak.KeepsAPlatformAlternativeAsAnOldLocation and the PlatformLanePatternRoles reason text stay open: this feature does not edit those files. Rejected: a Reports copy of the law (two owners of one rule) and one fixture per pattern (covers only remembered patterns).
facts.F2: The rules see the Reports move before any file moves, so the move in feature B cannot silently loosen a rule.
facts.F20: Layer rule, decided per file, never per type (a move never splits a file): a file is Domain if and only if it is not a port file and every top-level type it declares has IL edges only to the kernel (Lighthouse.Backend.Models and its sub-namespaces), the BCL and types of other Reports Domain files. A port file declares an I-prefixed port interface and stays in Application with every record and enum it declares; the flag is a declared fact on the map. A non-Domain file under Services/Implementation/Reports/Metrics is ApplicationMetrics (the grouping is kept); every other non-Domain file is Application. The check runs both ways: a Domain-listed file reaching beyond the kernel fails, and a kernel-only non-port file listed as Application or ApplicationMetrics fails. Expected Domain: ReportWindowPolicy, ReportCapPolicy, ReportSeriesReading; DailySeriesSummary reaches the Flow metrics Domain and stays ApplicationMetrics. If the IL makes a Metrics file kernel-only, the crafter returns it to the architect instead of choosing a layer.
